relevance_note: Case report of one PAMI syndrome patient with a PSTPIP1 variant: "Genetic testing revealed an E250K substitution of PSTPIP1".
method_note: Read by hand; JSON assembled by a short script from hand-chosen values. One in-scope person (the single case-report patient, label 'patient'). The literature review summarises 52 cases (Table 1, group counts only) with individual data in Table S1, which is not in the converted text, so no review patients get rows; 52 is recorded as n_patients_reported and cohort_size_as_stated. The patient's MEFV variant is recorded as printed ('MEFV1', E148Q); its zygosity is not stated for her (the Discussion statement on E148Q heterozygosity is general), and the authors note E148Q heterozygosity 'is not associated with a clinically meaningful phenotype in children' without classifying her variant. PSTPIP1 pathogenicity 'pathogenic' comes from the Introduction sentence naming p.E250K as a pathogenic variant. Variant type left 'not reported' ('substitution' is not a listed class). Age 18 years is the age at presentation to dermatology; follow-up continued after that, so it is an approximate last-evaluation age. Vital status not stated explicitly (left not reported). Inflammatory cysts of the groin/suprapubic area are not called abscesses, so the abscess checklist item is left not reported. Pathergy row rests on the Discussion sentence 'As seen in this case, history of pathergy may be present' plus the case text on flares at injection sites. Normal ferritin recorded as excluded elevated ferritin (D-27). No contradictions found.

treatment_summary.value: systemic corticosteroids, cyclosporine, colchicine, tacrolimus, tofacitinib, anakinra and canakinumab before presentation; canakinumab 150 mg increased to 300 mg every 4 weeks with tofacitinib 5 mg twice daily; intralesional triamcinolone (minimal improvement); topical clobetasol; switched to adalimumab 40 mg every 14 days with improvement; prednisone weaned to 2 mg daily; surgical removal of suprapubic cyst and gluteal keloid
span: the patient had been treated with varying doses of systemic corticosteroids and assorted combinations of immunosuppressive therapy comprising of cyclosporine, colchicine, tacrolimus, tofacitinib, anakinra, and canakinumab
Intralesional triamcinolone 10 mg/mL was injected into an inflammatory cyst on her right mons pubis with minimal improvement
canakinumab was increased to 300 mg every 4 weeks and topical clobetasol propionate ointment 0.05% was started

She was switched from canakinumab to adalimumab 40 mg subcutaneously every 14 days with improvement in her arthritis and psoriasiform dermatitis after only two doses. Tofacitinib 5 mg twice daily and prednisone 4 mg once daily were continued. The patient’s suprapubic inflammatory cyst and right gluteal keloid were successfully removed surgically.
Prednisone is slowly being weaned and she is currently on 2 mg once daily
